x: Our own Phil and Stephen were taking their share at the front with Phil Tedd and John McFarlane leading the Thames challenge and Jermain Mays loping along beside them.

John McFarlane of Thames was his only opposition as they dropped down out of the woods near the end of the first lap, but before the loop past the lake had been completed, Phil had pressed the accelerator gently to the floor and was away.

Men. 1 J McFarlane (TH&H) 40:30; gst R Ashe 41:01; 5 S Omar 41:47; 15 W Cockerell 42:49; 19 T Ellacott 43:35; 23 M Trees M40 44:01; 26 E Lyne 44:07; 47 T Hadfield 45:35; 63 S Zealey M40 46:47; 70 M Humphrey 47:05; 78 F Ward M45 47:48; 84 T Fordyce 48:25; 88 T O'Neill M50 48:48; 95 S Ryan 49:18; 133…
He did lead, on and off, over the first 2km but John McFarlane of Thames, twice previously in Phil’s slipstream this winter, was on form this time and pressing to move away himself.
Sure enough, with only 400 metres of the race gone, three men had already gained a 30 metre break - John McFarlane of Thames, Alistair Moses of Reigate and our own Phil.
Men. 1 J McFarlane (Thames H&H) 1:46:14; 6 T Hadfield 1:55:12; 14 J Wolf 2:01:13. Women. 1 H May (City of Bath) 2:02:52; 10 H Smethurst 4th W40 2:18:12.
